children: TD Cowen: Amazon (AMZN) posted five quarters of accelerating AWS growth, estimates AI-related business at a large annual run rate, expects constrained capacity through 2026–27 and doubling by 2027
Analysts raised Amazon (AMZN) price targets: Tigress Financial $385, TD Cowen $350, Rosenblatt $360, citing AI-driven growth and AWS strength as drivers for upside potential.
Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt says AI agents won’t hurt Amazon’s economics and sees ad pricing moving from CPC to CPA, noting Amazon can monetize transactions when AI agents help purchases.
Analyst Ivan Feinseth says Amazon (AMZN) has an integrated AI flywheel expected to accelerate AWS and AI growth, boost advertising, raise purchase frequency, and strengthen Prime engagement.
Amazon (AMZN) filed to raise at least $25 billion in U.S. bonds via eight floating- and fixed-rate tranches maturing from three to 40 years, per regulatory filings and July reports.
Amazon issued C$14 billion of Canadian-dollar notes, a record-size Canadian corporate bond deal, noting currency and principal as part of its debt-financing activity.
Amazon (AMZN) plans a six-part bond sale in Swiss francs, adding a new-currency tranche to its debt program to raise funds for operations and expansion.
Amazon (AMZN) cut more jobs in its restructuring, totaling about 30,000 layoffs through Jan 2026. CEO Jeff Bezos said earlier cuts were due to overhiring during the pandemic.
Amazon (AMZN) struck a six-year global streaming deal for the Emmys from 2027. Prime Video will exclusively stream the ceremony worldwide, free to viewers without a Prime subscription.
Amazon cut under 1,000 white‑collar roles mainly in its Stores unit. Affected teams: customer service, marketplace support, retail engineering and seller services across US, India and UK.
